name: Universidad Finis Terrae
overview:
IMPORTANT - Additional Programme Requirements


Students must demonstrate a B1 level in Spanish via an interview with a Spanish speaker prior to the choice selection period in order to be eligible for this destination (organized by IAFF team)


Finis Terrae University is a private Chilean university based in the capital Santiago. It was founded in 1988. It is one of the best universities in Chile with its Master Cycle accredited by the Chilean Ministry of National Education. This university has more than 4,000 students on an American-style campus in an upscale residential area of Santiago.

Santiago offers a unique mix of mountains, sea, and city life. In just one day, you can go skiing to the Cordillera de los Andes and later enjoy water sports at the beach—only 1.5 hours away! You can also go trekking or try paddleboarding on nearby lakes. There are amazing nature trails just outside the city.

As the capital, Santiago has great flight connections, making it easy to travel around Chile and South America quickly and easily.
administrative:
1. Application dossier

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline). If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet, please be patient.


In the past the partner has asked for the following:

  • Color photocopy of passport / residence card if you are a foreign student outside Europe (valid more than 6 months after return).
  • Application form (PDF)
  • A passport size photo
  • Your transcripts (PDF format)
  • A cover letter (in English or Spanish) explaining why you selected this university
  • Mobility/travel terms and conditions to sign (PDF)
  • Medical information sheet (word or PDF format)
  • International health insurance covering repatriation costs and taken out before departure to Chile (PDF format)
  • Surveys on your tastes and preferences in terms of courses to prepare your integration (Excel format)
  • Learning Agreement (allows you to select the courses you wish to follow) (PDF format)


To be given to Epitech bachelor campus administration to reenroll for the Tech4 (in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract.
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier.


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Visa

If your studies in Chile will last more than 6 months, you must apply for a Student Visa (Temporary Residence Permit – Student Subcategory). If your stay is less than 6 months, we still recommend applying for the student visa, but it's up to you.

Once you receive an acceptance letter from the university, you can start applying for a student residence visa according to the instructions given to you on the website of the Consulate of Chile in Paris, accessible here.


Chilean authorities generally require proof of sufficient financial means to cover the stay; as a reference, it is recommended to demonstrate access to at least 500 USD per month of stay (6,000 USD for 12 months).


Important notes:

  • Students who will not be able to present their visa before their departure will be automatically unsubscribed from the university.
  • Apply at least two months in advance to avoid delays.


Once you arrive in Chile, you will need to register your visa with the Policia de Investigaciones (PDI). You will also need to apply for a Temporary Identity Card at the Civil Registry (Registro Civil - RC) within 30 days of your arrival in the territory. Finis Terrae University will assist you in this procedure.


3. Insurance and Health

In Chile, healthcare is not free. Medical services are private and often very expensive.

It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student.


To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.


For more information, you can consult the country's health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/chili

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


Prepare your arrival

To find out more about advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the host country, click here.

accomodation:
On-campus accommodation

The university does not offer accommodation on campus.


Off-campus accommodation

The neighborhoods of Providencia and Las Condes are great areas to stay in — they are safe, lively, and have lots of services and amenities nearby. Keep in mind that the university is located near the Inés de Suárez metro station, and Santiago has an excellent public transportation system, so getting around the city is usually very easy and efficient.


Rent prices vary depending on the area, type of housing, and size. During the integration period, you can book an AirBnb and a hotel. You'll have time to visit the residences and select according to your preferences.


The housing options listed in the shared drive are suggestions based on providers who have previously accommodated international students, but they are not official partners of the university.


For additional resources, the university recommend to check platforms such as:

https://www.santiagoexchange.com/

https://www.livinnxsantiago.com/

https://fentastic.cl/
courses:
Credits

You must validate 30 credits per year, 15 per semester.


Academic Calendar

The semester starts at the beginning of August and ends in December.

The following semester starts in March and goes until July.


Department & Courses (approved by Epitech)

All courses are taught in Spanish.


Find below the courses list

  • INFORMÁTICA Y TELECOMUNICACIONES
  • Matematicas discretas (code 300) /6 credits
  • Sistemas Operativos (code 400) /6 credits
  • Algoritmos (course code 300) / 6 credits
  • Seguridad Informatica (code 400) / 6 credits


  • CIENCIAS DE LA INGENIERÍA
  • Microeconomia (code 200) / 6 credits
  • Bases de Datos (code 200) / 6 credits
  • Contabilidad Gerencial (code 200) / 6 credits
  • Programación (code 100) / 6 credits
  • Programación Avanzada (code 100) / 6 credits
  • Fundamentos de Ingeniería (code 100) / 6 credits


Course format and Workload

Please note that courses are mathematics/physics focused. We advise you to bring a calculator and a lab coat.

The university's engineering school, which provides computer courses, increasingly bases its teaching on praxis (50% based on projects), thus approaching the Epitech model.

You can find all the information provided by the university here.


Important Notes

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
cost:
Financial overview (4th Year EPITECH)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the application fees and part of the tuition fees.
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other expenses

  • Roundtrip flights: around 1100 € for an Air France direct flight.
  • Insurance: 300-600€/year depending on the provider & coverage level
  • Visa: 115€ (2025)
  • Administrative costs: 40€
  • School books/resources

Estimated monthly budget

The local currency is the Chilean peso. 1€ = 111 CLP (Rate - October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.

  • Housing 400$
  • Food and eating out150$
  • a baguette: 1$
  • a meal in a local restaurant: 8$
  • a coffee: 1,5$
  • Transport 40$
  • a metro ticket: 0,85$
  • Internet and phone 35$
  • Once you arrive, you’ll probably want a SIM card and internet right away. Start with a prepaid card, then you can switch to a plan with companies like Claro, Movistar, Entel, or Wom. If you’re staying over 90 days, you’ll need to register your phone. Do this with a provider or at www.multibanda.cl/ia
  • Leisure 100-150$

These prices are indicative and may vary.


Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

A market called VEGA Chica offers fruit, vegetables, cereals, and mate (traditional South American drink) at very affordable prices (supermarkets are much more expensive).
